subject: Post-call: ACME - structured output reliability & SDK next steps
messages:

Subject: Post-call: ACME - structured output reliability & SDK next steps

Hi Jared — great to meet today, and thanks for the time. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps for the integration track so your infra and app teams can validate structured output reliability end-to-end.

Call recap (high level):
- Goal: reliably generate constrained JSON from the model for downstream ingestion (order events, product catalog entries).
- Success criteria: >95% schema-valid responses in our integration tests; graceful fallback for invalid outputs; <200ms added end-to-end latency for structured calls.

Integration & architecture items we discussed:
1) SDK setup + auth
   - We’ll provide our Node and Python SDKs (attach redwood-sdk-setup.pdf). SDKs handle batching, streaming, and simple auth plumbing.
   - Auth options: API keys (short-term) or mTLS/STS if you want to integrate with your KMS/SSO.
2) Routing & model variants
   - You can route requests by policy: low-latency vs cost-optimized models. For critical structured output we recommend a latency-optimized variant with constrained decoding.
3) Structured output / tool-calling
   - Preferred pattern: model returns JSON that follows a schema (we provide example acme-sample-schema.json). Leverage function/tool calling when you need to invoke deterministic actions.
4) Embeddings + rerankers
   - Store short-term embeddings for reranking candidate responses when you have multi-step retrieval. We’ll share a sample pipeline.
5) Validation + retry patterns
   - Validate model output against JSON Schema locally. If invalid, retry with a targeted prompt (repair prompt) up to N times or fall back to a safe parser. See Dev’s note below for more details.

Next steps / owners:
- Dev (Dev Patel) to share a short technical playbook + sample schema and example SDK commands (attached). Target: 48–72h.
- Marissa (me) to coordinate a 30-min follow-up with your infra lead and our solutions team to walk through auth and routing. Proposed: Wed 25 Mar, 10:00 PT.
- Jared / Lina to confirm whether you want API-keys or SSO/KMS flow for auth and provide an infra contact.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-setup.pdf, acme-sample-schema.json

Thanks — I’ll let Dev follow up with the technical details.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME - structured output reliability & SDK next steps (technical playbook)

Hey Jared — quick technical playbook and specifics below. Attached: acme-sample-schema.json and redwood-sdk-setup.pdf. Also added a small example repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/tree/main/acme-integration

1) Auth options- API keys: easiest for PoC. Set X-Api-Key header or use SDK auth() helper.
- STS/KMS: we support token exchange flows. You can issue short-lived tokens from your IdP to Redwood via STS; SDK accepts bearer tokens. mTLS is supported for Private deployments — we can help set certs during onboarding.

2) SDK snippet (Node)
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ baseUrl: process.env.REDWOOD_URL, token: process.env.REDWOOD_BEARER });

const response = await client.generate({
  model: 'redwood-structured-v1',
  prompt: prompt,
  schema: './acme-sample-schema.json',
  max_retries: 2, // SDK-level retry on schema validation failure
});
console.log(response.structured_output);

3) Constrained decoding & tool-calling- Function/tool calling: when you declare a function schema, the runtime biases model generation to emit a function call that matches the signature — this is the most reliable route when you need structured fields.
- Token-level constraints: for some fields we emit constraint tokens (prefix/suffix tokens, allowed token vocab) and set low temperature to reduce noise. Works best for IDs/enums.

4) Validation + retry patterns
- Local JSON Schema validation: run ajv (or similar) against the returned JSON. If invalid, invoke SDK.generate with a targeted repair prompt that says: "The JSON is missing X — please return a valid JSON that matches the schema." Limit retries to 1–2 to avoid latency amplification.
- Repair-first fallback: if retries fail, fall back to a deterministic parser that extracts high-confidence fields (regex/heuristics) and flag the rest for manual review.
- Instrumentation: emit a validation result metric (valid/invalid, failure_reason) to Redwood Console so you can alert on regressions.

5) Embeddings & rerankers
- For multi-candidate generation, compute embeddings for each candidate and your context, then rerank using cosine similarity plus a confidence score derived from schema validation.

6) Eval harness
- We’ll include a small harness in the repo that: 1) runs N prompts, 2) validates responses against schema, 3) reports P(valid), avg latency, and suggested model/config tweaks.

If you want, we can pre-provision a sandbox API key and a short test dataset for you to run the harness — tell us preferred auth flow and infra contact.

Cheers,
